about: What the decision core relies on in Hermes, read from the pinned Hermes source, not guessed (07 section 11.2, step 0). Each fact names the file and line it was read from at the pinned commit. scripts/check-hermes-contract.py checks the VM against this file and changes nothing.

hermes.how_read: The tag v0.22.5 (also rc.3-v0.22.5) points at this commit in the upstream repository. It is the same commit the 29 Oct source audit used (07 section 1, `bf0203a7`). The VM's install is said to be v0.22.5 stable (02 'Built on 30 Oct'); the check script confirms the commit there.

profiles.states: Each Bot's gateway state for the phone's online dots is Hermes's own RuntimeState of that profile's gateway (absent, starting, ready, draining, incompatible, inaccessible, conflict), found the way the readiness check finds it and never started (room_send.py op states).

room.name: Thornswood Workbench
room.store: ~/.hermes/shared-state.db, table hosted_rooms (room_id, name, members_json, authority_gateway_id, authority_epoch, next_seq, revision, created_at, updated_at, disbanded_at)

room.transport: JSON-RPC methods groups.* on the gateway's native connection (the one Desktop uses through hermes serve); not on the api_server platform

payload.thread_id: required; Desktop sends the event id

send.idempotency: the gateway maps event_id to user:<sha256 of the key>, so the same key is the same event
send.only_kind: message.user; the actor is set by the gateway, never by the caller

read.event: {room_id, seq, event_id, kind, actor: {kind, id}, authority_epoch, payload, created_at}

room.client: The same user reaches the running gateway with hermes_cli.gateway_client.connect_gateway(endpoint=...) after hermes_cli.gateway_runtime.discover_gateway_endpoint (which never starts a gateway) and attachable(); groups.send's payload needs thread_id too (Desktop sends the event id), and its event id is user:<sha256 of the key>.

bot_chat.title: Bot Chat
bot_chat.one_per_profile: Bot Mode keeps one canonical, hidden session titled 'Bot Chat' per profile; a title is unique, so a second create collides. Look it up before creating.
bot_chat.transport: the api_server platform (loopback HTTP, default port 8642), per profile under /p/<profile>/, Authorization: Bearer <API_SERVER_KEY>
bot_chat.find: GET /p/<profile>/api/sessions?limit=200&title=Bot%20Chat&include_hidden=1, then the row whose title is exactly 'Bot Chat'
bot_chat.create_if_missing: POST /p/<profile>/api/sessions with exactly {title: 'Bot Chat', source}; any other field is refused (bot_chat_parameters_unsupported)
bot_chat.send: POST /p/<profile>/v1/runs with {input, session_id} and an Idempotency-Key header (1 to 255 characters); the same key replays the same run
bot_chat.uncertain: A timeout after the run was accepted means the message is already in the Bot Chat: never resend it. The core marks it effect.uncertain and reads the run back first (peer.py:355-366).
bot_chat.local_send: On the Bots' own machine, Hermes's message_agent sends to a Bot Chat with `hermes -p <profile> chat --in ~ -c 'Bot Chat' --create-if-missing -Q --query-file <file>`, as the same user; no API_SERVER_KEY and no api_server listener. The connector (step 4) uses this, so nothing in the gateway's settings changes. Only exit 0 is a confirmed send; anything else is unclear and never resent.
bot_chat.local_send_source: tools/bot_mode_dm.py:11-13 (transports), hermes_cli/_parser.py:237 --query-file and :285 --create-if-missing, hermes_cli/gateway_chat.py:374 (the query-file contract)
bot_chat.history_local: Each profile's ~/.hermes/profiles/<id>/state.db: sessions (id, title, archived, started_at) and messages (session_id, role, content, timestamp, active). The Bot Chat is the session titled 'Bot Chat'; read only, roles user and assistant, active rows.

own_chat.gateways: Besides the Bots' gateway (thornswood-bots), Patrick's Desktop picker shows my-hermes (his own Hermes on the VM, user patrick-hermes) and This device (his Hermes on One). The phone reaches both through own_connector.py, run as that Hermes's own user.
own_chat.home: Hermes keeps its state in ~/.hermes, or %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes on Windows, unless HERMES_HOME says otherwise; the chats are in state.db there.
own_chat.runtime: A launcher says how it starts its runtime: hermes --print-runtime-command prints a JSON list [python, "-I", "-c", bootstrap], the bootstrap ending in runpy.run_module('hermes_cli.main', run_name='__main__', alter_sys=True). On One that Python is in Hermes's own store and nothing lies beside hermes.exe; the readiness helper runs in the same bootstrap with runpy.run_path in place of that entry.
own_chat.runtime_source: hermes_cli/_launchers.py:39 runtime_command, :75 print_runtime_command, :481 the launcher's --print-runtime-command; hermes_cli/windows_ssh_runtime.py:363 (no python.exe beside a bin launcher is assumed)
own_chat.list: Read only from state.db: sessions with archived = 0 and hidden = 0, source not kanban, tool, oneshot (Hermes's own pickers leave these out) or subagent, not a sub-agent run (model_config $._delegate_from), and not a session that ended with end_reason 'compression' (a compressed chat goes on in a newer session, which is the one listed). Newest first by last_activity_at.
own_chat.turn: hermes chat -Q --format stream-json --query-file <file>, with --resume <session id> for a chat that is there, or --yolo --source cli --in <home> for a new one. stream-json prints one JSON object a line and ends with {type: result, session_id, exit_code, error?}; only exit 0 with exit_code 0 is a confirmed turn. --format stream-json runs through the gateway's own client (launch_gateway_chat).
own_chat.history: Full history pages back through state.db, read only: a chat's messages are those of its whole compression lineage (the sessions it went on from, each ended with end_reason 'compression', and those it goes on as), user and assistant, active = 1, not the compression summary (_compressed_summary = 1), ordered by Hermes's own message id. A resume of a compressed chat's id lands on the newest continuation (get_compression_tip), and a resume of a chat Hermes does not have is refused, never a new chat.
own_chat.history_source: hermes_state_sessions.py:46 _LINEAGE_CTE_SQL; hermes_state_common.py:531 (messages: id AUTOINCREMENT, active, _compressed_summary); hermes_cli/main.py:1357 _resolve_session_by_name_or_id (compression tip), :1543 a miss kept for "Session not found"; hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py:589 the resume aborts on a missing session
own_chat.resume_keeps_settings: A chat's launch settings (yolo, source, model, cwd and the rest of _POLICY) are frozen when the chat is made. A resume that passes one that differs is refused, and a resume that passes none keeps them. So --yolo and --source go only on a new chat, and a phone turn in a chat started elsewhere runs with that chat's own approvals.
own_chat.resume_keeps_settings_source: hermes_cli/gateway_chat.py:22 _POLICY, :202 the source of a new session, :297 check_resume_policy
own_chat.approvals: A gateway-admitted -Q turn is a finite turn, so approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode (default deny): a step that needs an approval is refused unless --yolo was frozen into the chat, or the chat has /yolo on. Hardline and deny rules run before yolo either way.
own_chat.ready: Whether that Hermes's gateway runs is asked without starting one, as for the Bots (room_send.py op ready, with profile empty).
own_chat.probe: The helper's quick ops (ready, react, session; the Bots' ready, states, send, react) run with HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1, Hermes's own switch that keeps a start from finishing an owed source update (dependency sync, launchers, product builds: minutes) before anything else, as Hermes's own probes run. A turn runs without it.
own_chat.probe_source: hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:343 prepare_launch (:371 why `gateway status` is spared it, :374 the switch); hermes_bootstrap.py:588 calls it at every start; hermes_cli/doctor_platform.py:541 and cron/scheduler_script.py set it for their probes
own_chat.busy: A message into a chat whose turn runs is handed over as Desktop's box hands it: config.get {key: busy, session_id} answers the chat's busy_input_mode, else display.busy_input_mode, else interrupt (queue for the TUI); steer is session.steer and interrupt is session.redirect, each {session_id, text, execution_generation}, answered queued, redirected or rejected, rejected meaning queue it as the next prompt; queue, a file, a slash command or a turn parked on a prompt is prompt.submit, whose receipt is started or queued. A resume's snapshot gives pending (each admission's status, started for the running one), prompts and execution_generation, and session.info events replace pending. `hermes chat` builds its view as hermes_cli.gateway_chat_view.GatewayChatView at run time, so room_send.py's turn puts a view in its place that changes only submit, then runs hermes_cli.main as Hermes's own launcher does.

reactions.store: Hermes keeps reactions on a message row, in messages.display_metadata under "reactions": a list of {emoji, author, at, seen?}, author "user" or "agent". Older rows carry the JSON as a string inside a string.
reactions.rule: One reaction per author per message (Tapback): set_message_reaction(session_id, row_id, emoji, author) with a different emoji replaces, the same emoji again takes it off, None takes it off, and a row outside the chat's visible lineage returns None.
reactions.write: In a process of Hermes's own, as Hermes's own user: hermes_state_registry.acquire(db_path or None) for the SessionDB (None is this user's own state.db; a profile's is ~/.hermes/profiles/<id>/state.db), then release_or_close. Hermes's own react_to_message tool does the same; Desktop's message.react calls the same set_message_reaction. room_send.py op react reads the reaction first and writes only when it differs, so asking twice never takes it off.

reactions.the_model: Hermes tells the model about Patrick's reactions once, on a later turn, as a note, and only when display.message_reactions is on in that Hermes's config.

tasks.asked: Patrick, 3 Nov: "I wanted to see the subagents, jobs, and background tasks on the Mobile and Desktop app", for Hermes, One and the six Bots. Each Hermes keeps them per profile, so the app's Tasks tab shows every profile at once.
tasks.live: Subagents and background commands live in the running gateway, so they are read from it, never started: session.active_list for the live chats (the same population as the live chat list; kanban, tool and oneshot chats left out), then subagent.list and process.list with each chat's session_id, the three Desktop's status stack polls. subagent.list gives the live roster (subagent_id, parent_id, depth, goal, delegation_id, model, started_at, status, tool_count, last_tool); a delegation_id marks a background child. process.list gives the chat's own background commands, running or ended (command as Hermes redacts it, status, exit_code, started_epoch, exited_at, completion_reason). A chat that closed between the list and its read answers not_found and is passed over. A gateway that is not running has none, and room_send.py says its state instead of an empty list.

tasks.jobs: Scheduled jobs are Hermes's cron jobs, kept per profile in <home>/cron/jobs.json. They are read with Hermes's own cron.jobs.list_jobs(include_disabled=True) inside that profile's home (set_hermes_home_override and use_cron_store), which is how Hermes's dashboard lists them for Desktop's Scheduled jobs page. Each job's name, schedule_display, state (effective_job_state), next_run_at, last_run_at, last_status and last_error (redacted as _format_job redacts it) are kept; a job whose latest execution is claimed or running is running now.

tasks.where: room_send.py op tasks, in a process of Hermes's own, as that Hermes's own user, with Hermes's switch that keeps a start from finishing an update (own_chat.probe). The Bots' connector asks it for the Bots every 30 seconds; each own connector asks it for its own Hermes (profile empty) every 20 seconds. The core keeps only the latest report of each, in memory (tasks.py).

control.asked: Plan Part 6 (2 Nov): a details pane beside an open chat of his own Hermes, as Desktop has, showing what Hermes holds for that chat and changing its model or thinking level, that chat only. Decision 4 A: only models his sign-ins, a free model or a local one covers are offered, so no change adds spend.
control.read: room_send.py op control opens the chat as Desktop does (session.resume), then reads session.info (model, provider), config.get reasoning (the chat's next-turn level), config.get busy (what a message sent while a turn runs does), config.get yolo (whether approvals are skipped in this chat) and model.options (Hermes's own picker list). The thinking levels offered are the ones the route's entry clamp accepts (route_supported_efforts).

control.change: A model and a thinking level each go through Hermes's own PreparedMutations.apply (session.mutate operation model, payload {model, provider}; operation reasoning, payload {effort}), fenced to the chat's revision and execution generation from session.resume, as Hermes's ACP adapter and TUI send them. Both are per-chat policy edits, never the profile's default. A model pick on a running chat is deferred to the next turn (status deferred) and is said so. A target Hermes's selection guard flags answers confirmation_required and writes nothing; no confirmation is ever sent from here, so it stays unswitched with Hermes's own words.

Nous Portal spends the plan's credits, so only its free models are offered. A model in a row's unavailable_models, or a row not authenticated, is never offered. sessions.rename: hermes sessions rename: SessionDB.set_session_title(session_id, title), the user's own title; it raises ValueError on a title another chat holds or one over MAX_TITLE_LENGTH (100), and the CLI refuses an empty title or one with a newline first. room_send.py op session, action rename, does the same, and does nothing when Hermes's sanitized title is the one asked for.

sessions.archive: Hermes's archive and bring back: SessionDB.set_session_archived(session_id, archived) hides or shows the chat and its whole compression lineage and keeps every message, as the TUI's session.archive does. An archived chat is not in Hermes's own chat lists (archived = 0 in own_connector LIST_SQL); a page of kind archived lists them.
sessions.delete: hermes sessions delete: SessionDB.delete_session(session_id, sessions_dir=<hermes home>/sessions, exclude_active_write_guards=True). It deletes the chat with its messages, its compression lineage (the parts it was compressed from) and its delegate children (side tasks), orphans a branch off it, and removes their session files. It raises SessionActiveWriteGuardError while a turn lease or compression lock holds it or a child, and RuntimeStoreError session_busy (a queued or running turn) or unknown_execution (a turn lost across a gateway restart; hermes sessions discard acknowledges it). It returns False for a chat that is not there, which the helper counts as done.
